/.h2: More Questions About Texas Football Uniforms

faqs.q: Do you ship custom football uniforms anywhere in Texas for free?
faqs.a: Yes. Shipping is free on every order, to every city in Texas, whether your program plays in the DFW Metroplex, the Rio Grande Valley or the Panhandle. See the Texas cities we deliver to for local timing.

faqs.q: How do we pay for a Texas football uniform order?
faqs.a: Payment is a single PayPal invoice, emailed to you once you have approved the design proof. Nothing is charged on the website, and nothing is charged for the quote or the mockup that come before that approval.

faqs.q: Can one football order cover game jerseys, practice gear and sideline layers?
faqs.a: Yes. Game uniforms, practice jerseys, sideline jackets, warm-up suits and fan gear can be ordered as one coordinated job, so colors, logos and number styles match across every piece instead of coming from separate vendors.

/all-categories/.h2: Questions About the Football Uniform Catalog

faqs.q: How many product families are in the football uniform catalog?
faqs.a: The catalog runs to 28 product families, grouped into jerseys, uniforms, practice gear, team packages and team apparel. Each family has its own page with its own fabric and sizing details, so you can compare them before asking for a quote.

faqs.q: Which football uniform category should a 7-on-7 team start with?
faqs.a: Start in the uniforms group, where 7-on-7 football uniforms use no-pads cuts and summer-weight fabric for the Texas summer circuit. Sizes on 7-on-7 builds run up to adult 4XL.

faqs.q: What separates football jerseys from full uniforms in the catalog?
faqs.a: Jerseys are tops only, from sublimated and reversible styles to blank and fan jerseys. Full uniforms pair the jersey with matching pants for youth, high school, college, 7-on-7 and flag programs, designed and approved as one set.

faqs.q: Are blank football jerseys useful when we add players mid-season?
faqs.a: They can be. Blank football jerseys exist for speed and flexibility, giving a program stock for new players without starting a full sublimation run. Mention your roster plans in the quote request and we will suggest where blanks fit.

faqs.q: Which catalog items are built for football practice rather than game day?
faqs.a: The practice gear group holds practice jerseys, padded football shirts, shorts, socks and gloves. They are built for daily contact, repeated washing and hot Texas sessions, and they can carry the same team colors as the game kit.

faqs.q: Does the football catalog include apparel for coaches and support staff?
faqs.a: Yes. The team apparel group covers coaches uniforms, warm-up suits, hoodies and sideline jackets, so staff on the sideline and players traveling to away games wear the same colors and logos as the uniforms on the field.

faqs.q: Can flag football programs find both jerseys and full uniforms here?
faqs.a: Yes. Flag football jerseys sit in the jerseys group and flag football uniforms in the uniforms group. Both use belt-friendly cuts for NFL Flag, rec divisions and UIL girls' flag, with sizes up to adult 4XL.

faqs.q: What is the difference between lightweight and sublimated football jerseys?
faqs.a: Lightweight jerseys are about fabric weight, built for camps, practice blocks and early-season heat. Sublimated jerseys are about decoration, with full-dye colors and graphics that cannot crack or peel. Many Texas programs order both for different parts of the year.

faqs.q: Are reversible football jerseys listed under jerseys or practice gear?
faqs.a: Reversible football jerseys sit in the jerseys group. They carry two team colors in one garment, which suits practice scrimmages, 7v7 and travel, and the second face is built to block the first color from showing through.

faqs.q: Do all football catalog categories share the same production turnaround?
faqs.a: Yes. Production runs one to two weeks after you approve the design, whatever the garment, from game jerseys to socks and sideline jackets. The clock starts at proof approval, so sending colors and roster details early protects your date.

/design-your-uniform/.h2: More Questions About Designing Your Uniform

faqs.q: What choices can I make when I design my uniform online?
faqs.a: You choose the garment, team colors, decoration, fabric, fit and roster size, and every option shown is a photo of a uniform we actually produce. The running price updates as you go, and one tap sends the specification to us.

faqs.q: Is tackle twill or embroidery priced in the online uniform designer?
faqs.a: No. The designer shows the published starting price, which includes full sublimation. Tackle twill, embroidery and sewn nameplates, along with heavier fabrics, are priced in your written quote so the number reflects the real build.

faqs.q: What happens after I send my uniform design from the designer?
faqs.a: A designer draws a free mockup in your colors, normally within 24 hours, and a written quote follows within one business day. Colors, numbers and logo position can still be revised, and nothing is cut or printed until you approve.

/blog/.h2: Questions About Our Football Uniform Guides

faqs.q: Which football uniform guide should I read before choosing jersey fabric?
faqs.a: Start with the football jersey fabric guide. It compares performance knits, mesh and sublimation against screen printing, and explains how Texas heat and contact level should shape the fabric you choose before you request a quote.

faqs.q: Do the football uniform guides cover youth and college differences?
faqs.a: Yes. The buyer's guide to youth, high school and college football uniforms explains how priorities shift with level, from forgiving sizing and value for youth leagues to durability for varsity and presentation for college programs.

faqs.q: Where can I learn how to plan names and numbers on jerseys?
faqs.a: The guide on custom names and numbers covers number legibility, name placement above the back number, consistent fonts across a roster and why sublimated numbers outlast heat-pressed ones over a hard season.

faqs.q: Is there a guide that lists everything a football team kit needs?
faqs.a: Yes. Building a Complete Football Team Kit walks through the core uniform, socks, gloves and base layers, sideline and warm-up apparel, and how to plan buffer stock and reorders so the kit stays consistent each season.

faqs.q: What does the custom football uniform design guide walk through?
faqs.a: How to Design Custom Football Uniforms covers choosing a primary color and accents, picking fabric and construction, planning names and numbers, collecting sizes and documenting the design as a system for future reorders.

faqs.q: Do the football uniform guides link to the products they discuss?
faqs.a: Yes. Each guide ends with a list of the product pages it refers to, so you can move from reading about sublimated jerseys or team kits straight to that product and then on to a quote.

faqs.q: Are the prices mentioned in the football guides final quotes?
faqs.a: No. Any price in the guides is the published starting price at the smallest order we produce, which is the highest per-piece tier. Your written quote prices your actual roster, decoration and fabric.

faqs.q: How recently were the football uniform guides updated?
faqs.a: Each guide shows its publish date and its last update, and all five were refreshed in September 2026. The update date sits next to the reading time at the top of every article.

faqs.q: Can I get a football uniform quote after reading the guides?
faqs.a: Yes. Send us your roster count and the date you need the uniforms, and a written quote and free mockup come back within one business day. You do not need a finished design to ask.

faqs.q: Which football guide helps a coach plan sizes across a roster?
faqs.a: Two help most. The design guide covers collecting accurate sizes and allowing for pads, and the youth, high school and college guide explains why a small buffer of common sizes saves rush reorders when players grow.

faqs.q: Does Texas Football Uniforms sell single jerseys at retail?
faqs.a: No. Everything is made to order against a team roster, so there is no single-piece retail sale. The whole process, from the mockup to the approval step, is built for someone buying on behalf of a team.

faqs.q: Do you make licensed NFL or college fan merchandise?
faqs.a: No. We do not sell licensed fan merchandise or resell another brand's gear. Every garment we make carries your own program's identity, with its colors, its logo and its players' names and numbers.

faqs.q: Can you print a school district or league logo on our uniforms?
faqs.a: Yes, with permission. If a logo belongs to a school district, a league or another third party, we need the program's confirmation that it may be reproduced before it goes into production.

faqs.q: Which decoration methods does Texas Football Uniforms use on team gear?
faqs.a: We use five decoration methods and choose them per garment rather than per order. Most Texas programs end up with full-dye sublimated football jerseys on the field and embroidery on staff layers, with tackle twill available as a stitched upgrade.

faqs.q: Why does Texas Football Uniforms decide the fabric before the design?
faqs.a: Fabric weight changes how a garment behaves in a Texas August more than any graphic choice does. Settling the build first, whether game-weight polyester or practice mesh, means the design is drawn for the fabric the team will actually wear.

faqs.q: Who are the main customers of Texas Football Uniforms?
faqs.a: High school programs ordering varsity and JV around the UIL calendar are the largest group. We also outfit youth and rec leagues, 7-on-7 clubs, flag programs, college club and camp teams, and coaching staffs who want the sideline to match the field.

faqs.q: What production window does Texas Football Uniforms work to?
faqs.a: Production runs one to two weeks after you approve the design, whatever the garment. Shipping is free on every order to every city in Texas, and rush requests are confirmed against your date before you order.

faqs.q: Why does Texas Football Uniforms ask for a size breakdown at checkout?
faqs.a: The cart is built for a full team order with a mixed size run, not a single shirt, so it asks how many of each size you need. That breakdown is what the production run is cut against.

faqs.q: When can we still change our design during a Texas Football Uniforms order?
faqs.a: At the proof stage. Color values, number size, nameplate spacing and logo position are all still editable before you sign off, which makes it the cheapest place for revisions. Once you approve, production starts.

faqs.q: Do Texas Football Uniforms practice jerseys use different fabric from game uniforms?
faqs.a: Yes. Game uniforms use 220gsm polyester with stretch mesh zones, while practice jerseys and pinnies are built in heavy-duty mesh for daily contact through two-a-days. Many programs order a separate practice run rather than wearing game gear in practice.

faqs.q: How quickly will Texas Football Uniforms reply to a quote request?
faqs.a: Quote requests are answered within one business day, and the free mockup normally arrives within 24 hours of the brief. Neither costs anything, and neither commits your program to an order.

faqs.q: What details should we include in a football uniform quote request?
faqs.a: Send the roster count, your team colors and the date you need the uniforms on the field. The more of that you include, the more likely the first reply is a real quote rather than a list of follow-up questions.

faqs.q: Can we reach the football uniform team by WhatsApp instead of the form?
faqs.a: Yes. Phone, WhatsApp, email and the quote form all reach the same desk, so use whichever suits your staff. The reply carries the same written quote and free mockup either way.

faqs.q: Should we send parents the size chart before contacting you about uniforms?
faqs.a: It helps. Sending parents the youth and adult size chart before you collect sizes means the size sheet comes back once rather than three times, and your quote can be priced against the real size run.

faqs.q: Do we have to talk to someone before ordering football uniforms?
faqs.a: No. You can order straight from the site and settle it against a PayPal invoice we email once you approve your design proof. Getting in touch first is there for programs that would rather discuss the order before committing.

faqs.q: Can we send our football uniform spec through the online designer instead?
faqs.a: Yes. The online football uniform designer collects the garment, colors, decoration, fabric, fit and roster details and sends them through in one tap, which gives us everything a written message would.

faqs.q: Is there a charge for a football uniform quote or mockup?
faqs.a: No. Both the written quote and the design mockup are free, and neither commits you to anything. Production only begins after you have approved the proof, and payment comes by PayPal invoice after that approval.

faqs.q: Do we need finished artwork before contacting you about football uniforms?
faqs.a: No. A first message does not need to be complete. A photo of last year's jersey is enough to work from, and the remaining details can be settled while the artwork is being drawn.

faqs.q: Should we include our first game date when contacting you about uniforms?
faqs.a: Yes. Production runs one to two weeks after you approve the design, so the date you need the uniforms on the field is what we plan the run around. Rush requests are confirmed before you order, not after.

faqs.q: What happens after we send a football uniform inquiry?
faqs.a: We reply with a written quote that prices your actual roster and a free mockup showing your colors, numbers and logo placement. You review it, ask for revisions if needed, and approve before anything is printed.

faqs.q: How do I measure a player's chest for a football jersey?
faqs.a: Measure around the fullest part of the chest, under the arms, with the tape level and arms down, without pulling tight. Measure over a t-shirt, and add two inches if the jersey will go over shoulder pads.

faqs.q: Where should football pants sit when measuring a player's waist?
faqs.a: Measure around the natural waist where the pants will sit, not the hips or the belt line of shorts. Football pants sit higher than casual trousers, and the hip reading matters more on integrated pants because the pad pockets sit there.

faqs.q: Do pro-cut and compression football jerseys follow the standard size chart?
faqs.a: They run closer to the body than a standard cut. Sizing for a specific style is confirmed at the mockup stage, and we tell you whether to move up or down before the order is placed rather than after it ships.

faqs.q: When do I need a sleeve measurement for a football order?
faqs.a: Only for warm-up jackets and coaches uniforms. Measure from the center back of the neck, across the shoulder and down the outside of the arm to the wrist, with the arm slightly bent.

faqs.q: Does tackle twill numbering cost more on custom football jerseys?
faqs.a: Yes. Full sublimation is included in the starting price, while tackle twill numbering, embroidery, applique, sewn nameplates and captain patches are stitched work that adds labor per jersey. Your quote prices the decoration you actually choose.

faqs.q: Which fabrics can we choose for custom football jerseys?
faqs.a: Jersey builds include birdseye mesh, lightweight interlock and premium performance polyester. Heavier game-weight knits, 4-way stretch compression fabric and dazzle finishes are available too, and they change the price per jersey in your quote.

faqs.q: What fabric weight do full custom football uniform sets use?
faqs.a: Uniform sets are built on 220gsm game-weight polyester with stretch mesh and ventilated panels. Integrated pad panels and heavier knits are available as upgrades and are priced in the written quote.

faqs.q: Can a football uniform order include home, away and alternate looks?
faqs.a: Yes. Uniform layouts are planned for consistency across home, away and alternate sets, with the same front, back and sleeve number structure. Each different design is counted and priced as its own run.

faqs.q: What decoration holds up on football socks, gloves and practice tops?
faqs.a: Practice items take sublimation, heat transfer and knit-in detailing, chosen per product. Socks and gloves suit different methods than practice jerseys, so we pick the one that will hold up to daily washing and contact.

faqs.q: Do football practice jerseys help coaches separate units during drills?
faqs.a: Yes. Color-coded practice tops make unit separation and roster identification simpler during drills and camp days. Reversible jerseys are another option when coaches want two colors in one garment for scrimmages.

faqs.q: Do football team packages come in youth and adult sizes?
faqs.a: Yes. Full roster package builds run from youth XS through adult 5XL, so a program can put a youth squad and a varsity roster into one coordinated package while keeping the same names, numbers and graphics.

faqs.q: How is a football team package priced per set?
faqs.a: Packages are priced per set, starting at the published price for the smallest order we produce. Larger rosters pay less per set, and stitched decoration or heavier fabric changes the number in your written quote.

faqs.q: Which fabrics are used for football hoodies, jackets and warm-up suits?
faqs.a: Team apparel is made in fleece, tricot, softshell and performance knit, depending on the piece. The fabric is matched to whether the garment is meant for warmth, travel or sideline weather, and the quote states which one you are getting.

faqs.q: Is embroidery available on football coaches and sideline apparel?
faqs.a: Yes. Embroidery is the usual choice on staff layers, alongside sublimation panels and heat transfer on other pieces. Because embroidery is stitched work, it is priced in your written quote rather than included in the starting price.

faqs.q: How many Texas cities have their own football uniform page?
faqs.a: Twenty-three, covering the DFW Metroplex, Greater Houston, Central Texas, Greater San Antonio, South Texas, the Rio Grande Valley, West Texas and the Panhandle. Each city page covers the local districts, leagues and transit days.

faqs.q: Is shipping free to every Texas city on the football uniform list?
faqs.a: Yes. Shipping is free on every order to every city in Texas, from Dallas and Houston to El Paso, Amarillo and McAllen. Delivery timing varies with distance, which is why each city has its own page.

faqs.q: Can a team outside the listed Texas cities order football uniforms?
faqs.a: Yes. We outfit football programs in every corner of Texas, not just the listed cities. Tell us your team, colors and roster count, and the quote, free mockup and production process are the same.

faqs.q: Which Metroplex suburbs besides Dallas and Fort Worth are covered?
faqs.a: Alongside Dallas and Fort Worth, the DFW Metroplex pages cover Granbury, Arlington, Plano, Frisco, McKinney, Allen and Denton. Each one notes the local districts and leagues so an order can be planned around that area's season.

faqs.q: Are Katy and Sugar Land covered alongside Houston for football uniforms?
faqs.a: Yes. Houston, Katy and Sugar Land each have their own page, covering Houston's 6A football country and Fort Bend programs. Orders ship free and are planned around the date you need the uniforms on the field.

faqs.q: Which West Texas and Panhandle cities have football uniform pages?
faqs.a: El Paso, Midland and Lubbock carry the West Texas pages, and Amarillo covers the Panhandle. Longer delivery distances make it worth sending your roster and game date early, since production starts at proof approval.

faqs.q: Do Rio Grande Valley and South Texas teams get the same service?
faqs.a: Yes. McAllen anchors the Rio Grande Valley page, while Corpus Christi and Laredo cover South Texas. The free mockup, free shipping and production timeline match what a Dallas or Houston program gets.

faqs.q: Is Round Rock grouped with Austin and Waco for uniform delivery?
faqs.a: Yes. Round Rock sits in the Central Texas group with Austin and Waco, while San Antonio has its own page for Greater San Antonio programs. Each page lists the local districts, leagues and transit days that apply there.

faqs.q: Why do delivery times differ between Texas cities on the list?
faqs.a: Texas is a big state, so transit days from production to your field vary by region. Each city page carries the local districts, leagues and transit days, so a coach can see how far ahead to send the roster for a given game date.

faqs.q: Do the Texas city pages cover youth and 7-on-7 programs too?
faqs.a: Yes. City pages cover the full range we make, from UIL high school football uniforms to youth leagues, 7-on-7 clubs, flag programs and coaching staff apparel. The order process is the same in every city.

faqs.q: Should home and away football uniforms share one design system?
faqs.a: Yes. The guide recommends treating home and away versions, practice gear and sideline apparel as one system with shared colors, logo and typography, so every piece looks like it belongs to the same program.

faqs.q: How should team colors be checked before finalizing a uniform design?
faqs.a: Think about how the colors look under stadium lights and against your field, then lock them as exact color values. That way every reorder matches the first run instead of drifting shade by shade.

faqs.q: What football jersey fit problems does the design guide warn about?
faqs.a: A jersey that is too tight restricts movement, and one that is too loose looks sloppy and gets grabbed in play. The guide recommends collecting real sizes from every player and allowing for pads under the jersey.

faqs.q: Why does a football uniform's typeface matter as much as its colors?
faqs.a: A team name, mascot and one consistent typeface for names and numbers all reinforce identity. Applying that typeface everywhere, from custom team jerseys to warm-ups, is what makes a program look established rather than thrown together.

faqs.q: Does the design guide recommend different builds for different positions?
faqs.a: It does. Heavy-contact positions benefit from more durable weaves, while hot-climate teams want lighter, breathable knits. Reinforced seams and stretch where players need it separate a uniform that lasts a season from one that lasts years.

faqs.q: Why are polyester knits preferred over cotton for football jerseys?
faqs.a: Polyester performance knits pull sweat to the surface where it evaporates, while cotton soaks it up and gets heavy. They also resist stretching out of shape and hold printed color well, which is why serious teams default to them.

faqs.q: What is the trade-off with very open mesh football jersey fabric?
faqs.a: Very open fabrics run cooler but can feel less substantial and show more underneath. For teams that play in real heat, the guide still favors lightweight football jerseys with built-in ventilation, because a cooler player performs deeper into the game.

faqs.q: Does a tighter jersey knit give a cleaner print than open knit?
faqs.a: Yes. A smoother, tighter knit gives a cleaner print surface and a more premium feel, while a more open knit runs cooler. The guide suggests matching the knit to your climate and level of play first.

faqs.q: Can sublimation create edge-to-edge patterns on football jerseys?
faqs.a: Yes. Because sublimation dyes the design into the fibers, it allows full-color gradients and edge-to-edge patterns that printed numbers cannot. It also adds no heavy layer to trap heat, which matters in Texas.

faqs.q: Should contact-heavy football teams layer padded shirts under their jerseys?
faqs.a: Some contact-heavy teams do, adding padded football shirts under the jersey for extra protection. The guide advises settling durability and protection at the design stage, since reinforcing up front costs far less than replacing torn jerseys mid-season.

/blog/youth-high-school-and-college-foot.h2: More Questions on Uniforms by Level

faqs.q: Why do youth football uniforms need forgiving fits?
faqs.a: Kids grow fast, so youth uniforms need fits with room to grow and simple reorder options. Leagues are often volunteer-run on tight budgets, which makes easy-care, lightweight fabric and a clean, bold design the practical choice.

faqs.q: How many uniform combinations do college football programs usually need?
faqs.a: The guide describes home, away and alternate sets at the college level, plus matching sideline and travel apparel, all designed as one system. Multiple combinations and a television-ready look are the expectation there.

faqs.q: What uniform buying mistake does the youth to college guide warn against?
faqs.a: Buying above or below your real needs. That means over-spending on features a youth team will not use, or under-building a uniform that a varsity season will wear out. Match the order to the level and document the design.

faqs.q: Why should high school programs plan football uniforms across multiple seasons?
faqs.a: Documenting the design, buying quality construction and keeping some replacement stock lets a program using high school football uniforms look consistent year over year instead of piecing together mismatched gear as players cycle through.

faqs.q: Where do 7-on-7 uniforms fit across youth, high school and college?
faqs.a: Many programs at every level add 7-on-7 football uniforms for offseason play. Whatever the level, the guide suggests working backward from how the team plays and what the budget allows to land on the right uniform.

/blog/custom-names-and-numbers-on-footba.h2: More Questions on Jersey Names and Numbers

faqs.q: Should football jersey numbers have an outline on light-colored fabric?
faqs.a: An outline is worth considering on busy or light-colored fabrics, because it adds contrast and helps the number stand out. Pick number and name colors that contrast strongly with the jersey so legibility comes first.

faqs.q: Can football jersey numbers also go on the shoulders or sleeves?
faqs.a: Yes. Numbers usually go on the front and back, and often on the shoulders or sleeves as well. Getting placement and sizing right as part of the overall design keeps the jersey looking clean rather than improvised.

faqs.q: Which number font style suits a classic football jersey look?
faqs.a: Bold, blocky numerals give a classic look, while sharper typefaces feel more modern. Whatever you choose, use it on every jersey and every reorder, because the typography of names and numbers becomes part of the team's brand.

faqs.q: Do sublimated numbers make a football jersey lighter and cooler?
faqs.a: Yes. Sublimated numbers are dyed into the fabric rather than layered on top, so they add no weight or heat-trapping layer. Heat-pressed or sewn-on numbers sit on the surface and are more prone to lifting during a hard season.

faqs.q: How do we add player names across a whole football roster?
faqs.a: Plan the name style into the design system first, then apply the same font, size and placement to every player. Custom name football jerseys keep typography identical across the roster so personalization looks intentional rather than tacked on.

faqs.q: Why should the core uniform be settled before the rest of the kit?
faqs.a: The core uniform sets the colors, logo and typography that every other piece follows. Once those are locked on the home and away set, adding socks, layers and sideline apparel is a matter of applying the same system.

faqs.q: Which football team kit items need replacing most often?
faqs.a: The guide names finishing details like custom football team socks as the highest-turnover items. Building extra pairs into the first order means mid-season replacements do not need a separate reorder.

faqs.q: Can football team kit hoodies double as everyday school wear?
faqs.a: Yes. Coordinated hoodies are pieces players wear around school and town, extending the program's presence beyond game day. They work as both team branding and team pride in the same order.

faqs.q: Are base layers part of a complete football team kit?
faqs.a: Yes. The guide lists base layers and undergarments alongside socks and gloves as the smaller pieces that finish a kit. They keep players comfortable and stop the mismatched look of everyone wearing whatever they own underneath.

faqs.q: Do gloves need to match the rest of the football team kit?
faqs.a: They should coordinate with it. The guide treats gloves alongside socks and base layers as finishing pieces that cost little relative to how much they lift the team's unified look from head to toe.
